feeds.title: Ethics and Society Blog
feeds.description: Ethical analysis and news from the Fordham University Center for Ethics Education,The Master of Arts in Ethics and Society provides students with a cross-disciplinary foundation in the application of moral and ethical theory to social issues.

feeds.title: Animal Ethics Blog
feeds.description: Animal Ethics promotes respect for nonhuman animals through outreach, research, and education. They support and research interventions to improve the lives of animals in the wild, such as vaccinations and helping animals in natural disasters. They explore how future technologies will enable us to avoid catastrophic risks and ways technology can be used to help wild animals on a large scale. The blog features articles on seminar, conferences , animal related events, rights and more.

feeds.title: Impact Ethics
feeds.description: Founded in 2013, IE is managed by the Memorial University Center for Bioethics at Memorial University in St. John's, Newfoundland, and Labrador, Canada. IE is a forum for discussion of and commentary on bioethical issues, presenting a diverse range of voices and perspectives. IE has a preference for posting articles that are grounded in the current Canadian context, although we are willing to consider any well-written article that confronts an important bioethical issue.

feeds.title: Louisiana Legal Ethics
feeds.description: Louisiana Legal Ethics is a legal ethics blog of Prof. Dane S. Ciolino. Articles on reports and analysis of recent laws, regulations, cases, and administrative decisions relating to legal and judicial ethics in Louisiana.

feeds.title: Ethical Advocate Blog
feeds.description: Ethical Advocate provides comprehensive ethics and compliance solutions, including ethics and compliance training and confidential and anonymous hotlines, meeting Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), and other regulatory and reporting needs.

feeds.title: Primary Ethics
feeds.description: Primary Ethics was established to give schoolchildren the space to explore ethical dilemmas. They are an independent not-for-profit organization and the sole approved provider of ethics classes to NSW public schools. Their mission is to support children to develop skills in ethical reasoning, critical thinking, and respectful discussion by enabling community volunteers to deliver ethics classes in public primary school

feeds.title: The Ethics Centre
feeds.description: The Ethics Center is an independent not-for-profit that brings ethics to the center of everyday life through events, consulting, and counseling. Follow their blog to dive deep into features and extensive articles covering the latest ethical dilemmas, current events, breaking news, and philosophy.

feeds.title: Ethics Alarms
feeds.description: Ethics Alarms blog is a blog featuring valuable information in the form of articles on current events and issues. The blog is managed by Jack Marshall, who is an ethicist. The website is about ethics, defined as the study of right and wrong, and how to become better at telling the difference.

feeds.title: Ethics Unwrapped Blog
feeds.description: Ethics Unwrapped is a free educational program that presents the latest research in ethics with top experts and creative zing to make learning easy, memorable, and fun. This accessible, research-based program is used around the world by more than 1,200 colleges and universities, in hundreds of businesses and organizations, and by tens of thousands of ethics learners. They also have a blog spreading knowledge about ethics, decision-making, moral injury, and more.

feeds.title: Practical Ethics
feeds.description: At the Practical Ethics blog, you can find daily ethical analysis of news events from researchers in four centres based at the Philosophy.We focus on current events with practical ethical relevance, including developments in science and technology, environmental policy, public health, and information ethics.

feeds.title: Public Ethics
feeds.description: The Public Ethics blog offers expert philosophical analysis of ethical issues in the news. It is published by the Stockholm Center for the Ethics of War and Peace, and started life as the Ethical War Blog.

feeds.title: Business Ethics Journal Review
feeds.description: The Business Ethics Journal Review (BEJR) is an open-access academic journal publishing peer-reviewed commentaries and facilitating broad discussion. BEJR operates on a free, non-profit basis. There are no fees charged to anyone for anything. The goal of BEJR is to provide a forum for commentary on articles published in peer-reviewed business ethics journals. In this way, BEJR seeks to augment the existing system of scholarly publication.

feeds.title: Engineering Ethics Blog
feeds.description: The Engineering Ethics blog is a place for comments on current events with an engineering ethics angle. This blog discusses a much broader view of engineering ethics, and deal with subjects as diverse as disasters that involve technical matters, movies with an engineering ethics or technical angle, and even philosophical and religious questions that engineers might have to deal with.

feeds.title: The Guardian » Ethics
feeds.description: The guardian is the place to get all the latest US news, world news, sports, business, opinion, analysis, and reviews from their team, the world's leading liberal voice. The ethics page of the guardian provides valuable information on essential topics like the latest news and updates, political ethics news, artificial intelligence, government policies, and more.

feeds.title: Ethisphere Magazine
feeds.description: Ethisphere is the global leader in defining and advancing the standards of ethical business practices that fuel corporate character, marketplace trust, and business success. They have a blog that curates research, editorial, reports, and videos for ethics, compliance, and culture professionals from Ethisphere Magazine, our BELA community, the World's Most Ethical Companies, and our team.

feeds.title: The Business Ethics Blog
feeds.description: A blog about Business Ethics by Chris MacDonald, Ph.D. Chris is a writer, speaker, and consultant on ethics. A philosopher by training, he teaches at Ryerson University's Ted Rogers School of Management, and is a Nonresident Senior Fellow at Duke University's Kenan Institute for Ethics. He is co-editor of the Business Ethics Journal Review.

feeds.title: Media Ethcis
feeds.description: Media Ethics is the Magazine Serving Mass Communication Ethics. They feature interesting topics on 21st-century people, trauma, journalism, artificial intelligence, cancel culture, and many more trending issues.

feeds.title: Business Ethics
feeds.description: Business Ethics is an online magazine with a strong heritage in the fields of ethics, governance, corporate responsibility, and socially responsible investing. The mission of Business Ethics is to promote ethical business practices and to serve that growing community of professionals and individuals striving to work and invest in responsible ways. They seek to do that by offering their readers information, opinions, and cutting-edge analysis about business and the intersection of business and society.

feeds.title: EJN » Inside Ethics Blog
feeds.description: The Ethical Journalism Network aims to strengthen the craft of journalism and to promote for the public benefit high ethical standards in media through education, training, and publication of useful research. The networks inside the ethics blog feature information on the latest news, daily updates, medical, mental health, finances and more.

feeds.title: Ethics and Culture Blog
feeds.description: Ethics and Culture is a blog by Andrew J. Spencer where he gives out his thoughts, reviews, and commentary on the ethics and culture of the world and talks about the changes he wishes to bring through his blog.

feeds.title: Business Ethics Highlights
feeds.description: Business Ethics Highlights bring you the day's business news as it relates to business ethics. They also occasionally post links to professional and scholarly conferences related to business ethics and jobs in the field. They feature Business Ethics News, Curated by Chris McDonald & Alexei Marcoux.

feeds.title: University Policy Blog
feeds.description: The Office of Ethics and Policy was created in 2016 by Chancellor Carol Folt. Their mission is to promote a culture of transparency and accountability through policy and integrity initiatives. Their blog features interesting and helpful articles on important topics like Big Lessons from Bad City, Truth, courage, higher education, values, and more.

feeds.title: ERLC
feeds.description: The Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission is an entity of the Southern Baptist Convention. The ERLC is dedicated to engaging the culture with the gospel of Jesus Christ and speaking to issues in the public square for the protection of religious liberty and human flourishing. Our vision can be summed up in three words: kingdom, culture and mission. The commissions blog is highly informative and delivers news of the latest events and also features articles on self improvement.

feeds.title: Ethico
feeds.description: Founded in 1997 by a group of experienced E&C consultants, Ethico began under the name of Compliance Concepts. The hotline service which would become Ethico was created to fill a need for compliance programs that were frustrated with poor hotline quality. In the beginning, there was a primary focus on serving healthcare organizations. The Ethico Blog features articles on speak-up culture, case management, unethical behavior, workplace improvement, and similarly important matters.

feeds.title: Ethics Sage
feeds.description: Ethics Sage is directed by Dr. Steven Mintz. Steve shares insights into business ethics through his Workplace Ethics Advice blog and a special take on ethics in colleges and universities in a new blog, Higher Ed Ethics Watch, that begins next month. In his blogs, he gives a critical analysis of ethical dilemmas encountered in daily life and shares his wisdom on all things ethical.
